transcript.text: Did anyone watch the game last night? Bayes' theorem lets us flip a conditional probability around. The posterior is proportional to the likelihood times the prior. A Type I error is rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true. The central limit theorem says sample means are approximately normal for large samples. Remember, the p-value is not the probability that the null is true. The variance of a sum is the sum of the variances for independent variables.
